title: Canadian Supreme Court sets date for hearing on parental rights law
description: OTTAWA ( LifeSiteNews ) — In March 2027, Canada’s Supreme Court will hear appeals made by a pro-LGBT group over a Saskatchewan law requiring parental consent to be obtained before children use different pronouns at school. According to Eric Freeman, a lawyer for UR Pride, the hearing in the nation’s top court will begin on March 22, 2027. … As for Bill 137, it was passed and became law in 2023. Known as the “ Parental Inclusion and Consent Policies ,” it also includes provisions which allow parents to opt their kids out of sex-ed and third-party presentations from groups such as Planned Parenthood. After the bill became law, UR Pride challenged it in a provincial court. A judge ruled in favor of UR Pride, which led Saskatchewan Premier Scott Moe to announce that he would use the government’s notwithstanding clause to protect the legislation from the courts. A survey from 2023 shows that 86 percent of Saskatchewan participants want parental rights codified in law and support the premise of Bill 137.

title: Abortion pill kills Canadian woman and her unborn baby
description: ( LifeSiteNews ) — A Canadian woman and her unborn child are dead after taking an abortion drug purchased overseas, court records show. The 31-year old woman, from Lethbridge, Alberta, died after taking the abortion drug in 2024. So did her child. She had ordered the drug from the Philippines, which was an unknown “medication,” and took the pill on June 10, 2024. … Health Canada’s adverse-reaction database contains more than 100 reports of serious harm to Canadian women since the drugs became available in 2017, but thousands more have gone unreported. The Campaign Life Coalition described the Lethbridge deaths as “a tragic story made possible because women have been lied to that abortion drugs are safe when they are not.” “It’s time to ban abortion drugs in Canada. Too many dead mothers and way too many dead preborn babies,” said Baklinski.
